FN-AKD87SQ-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 79
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Senator Rodger Smitherman
Analyst: Hunter Lapp Date: 03/05/2024
Senate Bill 79 as introduced would increase the administrative obligations of occupational
licensing boards by an undetermined amount by: (1) requiring the boards, upon request, to make
a determination of whether an individual’s criminal conviction would disqualify an individual
from obtaining the occupational license being sought; and (2) authorizing the boards to adopt
rules to implement the provisions of this bill. Additionally, this bill would allow the boards to
charge up to $20 per request to offset the administrative cost of making this determination.
This bill would also repeal existing law requiring an individual convicted of a felony and
seeking to obtain an occupational license to petition the circuit court to obtain an Order of
Limited Relief and pay a $100 filing fee, which would reduce the Administrative Office of the
Courts (AOC) administrative obligations of, and administrative filing fee receipts collected from
petitioners for Orders of Limited Relief. Per AOC, since 2019, there have been 11 petitions for
Orders of Limited Relief for a total, of $1,100.
Further, this bill would reduce receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, and
other funds to which court costs paid by persons petitioning the court for relief would normally
be deposited.

FN-AKD87SQ-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 79
Committee: Boards, Agencies and Sponsor: Senator Rodger Smitherman
Commissions
Analyst: Hunter Lapp Date: 04/01/2024
Senate Bill 79 as passed the Senate would increase the obligations of occupational licensing
boards by an undetermined amount dependent upon the cost to: (1) make a determination of
whether an individual’s criminal conviction would disqualify an individual from obtaining the
occupational license being sought, upon request; and (2) adopt rules to implement the provisions
of this bill. This increase in obligations could be offset, wholly or partly, by the collection of a
fee of up to $20 per request to offset the administrative cost of making this determination.
This bill would also repeal existing law requiring an individual convicted of a felony and
seeking to obtain an occupational license to petition the circuit court to obtain an Order of
Limited Relief and pay a $100 filing fee, which would reduce the Administrative Office of the
Courts (AOC) administrative obligations of, and administrative filing fee receipts collected from
petitioners for Orders of Limited Relief. Per AOC, since 2019, there have been 11 petitions for
Orders of Limited Relief for a total of $1,100.
Further, this bill would also reduce receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, and
other funds to which court costs paid by persons petitioning the court for relief would normally
be deposited.
